tour.overview:
Inside the ancient volcano of Tahiti Nui, the Papenoo valley cuts deep into the island, its walls streaked with waterfalls and covered in rainforest. A track built for a hydroelectric project crosses the island through the valley, past archaeological sites, to the Relais de la Maroto, a former workers' lodge, and the Vaihiria lake in a crater on the other side.

This private 4x4 day takes you into this wild interior with a local guide, a world away from the beaches.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Tahiti
• Type: private 4x4 with local guide and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; bumpy track

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Papenoo valley and its waterfalls.
• The Farehape marae.
• The Relais de la Maroto.
• The Vaihiria crater lake.

WHY THIS WORKS
The track is only passable by 4x4; your guide knows the plants, the legends and the archaeological sites of the valley.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, adventurous families and photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the coast, choose our Tahiti circle island tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
After heavy rain the river fords can close the track; the tour is then adapted. Bring swimwear and insect repellent.

days.name: The Papenoo valley, its waterfalls, the Farehape marae, lunch at the Maroto and the crater lake
days.description:
What to expect: Tahiti's wild interior by private 4x4, with a local guide and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and drive east to the mouth of the Papenoo river. The track follows the river into the valley, crossing it at fords, while waterfalls stream down the green cliffs on both sides; after rain there can be dozens. Your guide points out wild plants used in traditional medicine and food, such as ginger, guava and mape chestnut trees.

You stop at the marae of Farehape, a restored archaeological site where the ancient people of the valley lived and worshipped, and swim in a natural pool beneath a waterfall. Lunch is at the Relais de la Maroto, a lodge in the heart of the island built for the hydroelectric project.

If the track is open, you continue up through a tunnel to Lake Vaihiria, a lake in an old crater surrounded by forest, home to eels, before returning down the valley to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:15 – Entrance to the Papenoo valley.
10:30 – Waterfalls and a natural pool.
11:30 – Farehape marae.
12:30 – Lunch at the Relais de la Maroto.
14:00 – Lake Vaihiria (if open).
15:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The track can close after heavy rain.
• The full crossing to the south coast can be arranged.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and driver, local guide, lunch, fruit, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the 4x4 private?
faq.answer: Yes, a private vehicle with driver and guide.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, at the Relais de la Maroto.

faq.question: Can we swim?
faq.answer: Yes, in natural pools when conditions allow.

faq.question: What if it rains?
faq.answer: Light rain makes the waterfalls more spectacular; after heavy rain, the fords may close and we adapt.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children over about 5. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Not really; the track is bumpy and some stops require walking on uneven ground.

faq.question: Are there mosquitoes?
faq.answer: Yes, in the valley; bring repellent.

faq.question: Can we cross the whole island?
faq.answer: Yes, on request, ending on the south coast.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, swimwear, shoes that can get wet, insect repellent and a rain jacket.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May to October, the drier season.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in French Polynesia and is never expected, but a small gesture for excellent service is always appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
